note: Reviews that concluded the articles needed no change. Editing an article is the ordinary evidence of a review; this records the outcome that cannot be expressed by editing, because there was nothing to edit. Every entry PINS the content it reviewed — a digest of each locale's title, summary and body — so a review of an article that has since changed is stale and stops counting. Append only, and every entry must say what was reviewed and why nothing changed.

reviews.reason: UX redesign pass: a field's purpose now reads above its control instead of below it, on worker onboarding and the customer address form. Ordering and spacing only. Every statement these articles make about what is required, what is kept, and what Warsha does with an address remains true, and all three were already reviewed earlier the same day.

UX redesign pass: form labels, helper lines and error lines moved from the caption step to bodySmall after measuring them at 16dp on the Arabic sign-in at 320dp; the create-account button on sign-in made full width to match the primary above it; the gateway's spare vertical space redistributed. Type sizes, widths and spacing only. Nothing either article states about signing in, recovering a password, or what the first screen offers has changed.

The work picker stopped showing category headings, and this article said kinds of work in the same area sit under one heading. That sentence described behaviour that no longer exists, so it was corrected in all three locales to say they sit together in the list. The rest of the article was read again against the rendered picker while making the change: the question it quotes, the ten-selection limit, the work-versus-person explanation and the order of the onboarding steps all still match what the screen does.

Presentation pass on the application sign-in and signup screens: Forgot password, Resend confirmation, Create one and Sign in stopped being underlined anchors and became compact controls, at the same size, in the same positions, going to the same routes. The legal links inside the consent sentence were deliberately left as inline links. The sign-in lead also dropped the sentence "Warsha works out the rest". Both articles refer to these controls by name and by position — "Use Forgot password to request a recovery link", "Sign in sits below the two cards" — and never by widget type, so every statement they make is still true.

Accessibility-only change on the professional verification screen: three checkboxes that drew their own icon and label — the Skill Certificate question, the criminal-record confirmation and the payout ownership confirmation — were given explicit accessible names. With none, Android composes a name from the children and the decorative icon contributes an empty first segment, so each announced itself with a missing opening word. No behaviour, no visible copy, no field, no requirement and no lifecycle changed; what these controls do, what they require and what they record is exactly as both articles describe.

Two location changes reviewed together. The mapless confirmation: when the renderer cannot draw, its route withdraws and the resolved address is confirmed in words instead of behind a dead map frame. And a decision record tracing what the server actually requires — coordinates, enforced by confirm_my_service_address, which is why geocoding failure stays a recoverable block rather than a degraded completion. Neither changes what either article states: the same location information is required, obtained the same three ways, stored and validated identically, and the customer address flow is untouched. What changed is that a map which cannot paint no longer looks like a failure to find the address.

Accessibility naming pass over the order card, booking detail actions, quote submission, invitation rows, chat report dialog and notification rows. Controls that were composing their own accessible name from their children now carry an explicit one, decorative icons were marked decorative, and two inline actions a screen reader could never reach - rate this job, and mark read or archive a notification - are offered as accessibility actions on the row that already contained them. No visible copy, no on-screen control and no step of any flow changed; the same actions are in the same places doing the same things. Both articles describe what the flows do and what changes a booking, and neither describes control labels, icons or assistive technology, so nothing either article states became untrue. Reviewed the English text in full against the change; the Arabic and French carry the same statements, which test:help-language-parity holds them to.

Marketplace matching and distance change (202609160001): requests are now matched by the Professional's declared service area, the work-location step records a private matching anchor and is no longer saved as a default address, discovery returns no distance, and the customer quote sort Closest was removed. Read both articles in English, Arabic and French against that change. The addresses article describes naming an address, confirming its pin, the official governorate and area lists, and draft persistence; it makes no statement about defaults for professionals, matching, or distance, so nothing in it became untrue. The requests article describes posting a request, comparing quotes by amount, timing, message, materials, payment methods, rating and verification, cancellation, and jobs; it never lists Closest or any distance among the comparisons, and says matching professionals may quote, which remains true. The Professional-facing articles that did describe location and matching were edited in the same change.

Account deletion requests are now carried out (202609170009): an elapsed waiting period is judged against the blockers and an approved request is anonymized, erasure empties an address of the precise place, and sign-in is revoked. Both articles were read against that change. Neither describes deletion: what a request and a quote are, and the Professional opportunity and job lifecycle, are unchanged by it. The deletion behaviour is documented in customer-account-security and worker-getting-started, updated the same day. The impact rule matched because the migration filename carries the word request.

A Professional may now cover more than one district: the native onboarding and profile editors and the web profile editor add, list and remove service areas and refuse a repeat, while the work location stays one place; place names in those editors are shown in the reader's language from the official list (egyptPlaceNames), and Mock signup now creates the Professional profile as the server does. All three articles were read in English, Arabic and French against that change. worker-onboarding-verification described a single governorate and district, which became untrue; its service-area paragraph now says to add every district worked in, that a request from a district not added does not reach the Professional, that one can be removed, and that the work location stays one place (en/ar 10, fr 9). worker-getting-started already says to set service areas, in the plural, and nothing in it became untrue. customer-addresses-location says governorate and area come from the official list, which still holds; showing a stored name in the reader's language makes no statement in it untrue.

Reviews reached the web (the Customer's review of a completed job under My jobs, with photos and editing; the Professional's one reply on their job), both surfaces now read one review copy (French corrected where it said different things), and the phone's review edit, which had never reached the server, was fixed. customer-requests-quotes-jobs and worker-opportunities-jobs said nothing about reviews; each gained a paragraph in English, Arabic and French stating what is true on both surfaces: the scores, words, photos and anonymity; a limited, shown edit window; one unchangeable reply; reporting from the app; and that only visible reviews count. admin-reported-reviews was read against the same change and nothing in it became untrue.

A Professional's reviews can now be read, voted helpful and reported on the website, from their card on the discover page (the web's Find help / دوّر على صنايعي / Découvrir), through get_provider_reputation_summary, vote_review_helpfulness and report_review. customer-requests-quotes-jobs said reporting was in the app only, which became untrue; the paragraph now says where reviews are read and reported on each surface, naming the page as the reader sees it in English, Arabic and French.
